description: An image that crumples like real paper when you hold it; you can drag it, and on release it either unfolds or keeps its creases, depending on your choice.
interactionNotes: Grab the paper with the mouse and hold it; it crumples in your hand like real paper, tilting and following you as you move. On release, depending on the "release behavior", it either fully unfolds or keeps a crease from the memory of being crumpled. With the keyboard: hold Space or Enter to crumple, move it with the arrow keys (hold Shift for faster) and reset with Escape. With `prefers-reduced-motion`, all transitions become instant.

props.src: URL of the image the paper is built from. Required; the remote image must allow CORS.
props.alt: Alternative text for the image — used both for the fallback `` and in the button's screen-reader label.
props.backSrc: Image for the back of the paper. If omitted, the paper's back is `paperColor`.
props.width: Paper width, in pixels. Together with `height` it sets the paper's aspect ratio.
props.imageFit: How the image fits on the paper.
props.releaseBehavior: What happens after release: stay crumpled, fully unfold, or unfold while keeping some creases.
props.crumpleAmount: How much it crumples, 0 to 1. Holding longer does not increase it — it is the fixed target of the spring.
props.releaseDuration: Unfold duration after release, in seconds.
props.foldCount: Number of fold guides; more means finer creases. 3 to 16.
props.foldSharpness: Crispness of the edges; 1 is like an ironed fold, 0 is soft and wavy.
props.wrinkleDepth: Depth of the wrinkles; above 1 is exaggerated.
props.creaseStrength: With `releaseBehavior="creased"`, how much of the crumpling stays in the paper.
props.paperColor: Color of the paper's back and edges; the front is the image, so it is mostly visible inside the folds.
props.roughness: Surface roughness for lighting; 1 is fully matte.
props.paperTexture: Intensity of the paper grain (fine bump).
props.lightIntensity: Directional light intensity; zero means ambient light only.
props.lightAngle: Light angle, in degrees; light comes from this side so the folds cast shadows.
props.shadow: Enable a soft shadow under the paper.
props.draggable: While holding, the paper moves with the pointer.
props.dragRotation: How much it tilts while dragging, in degrees; maximum 60.
props.dragRadius: Movement radius from the center, in pixels.
props.returnToOrigin: Return to the center after release (unless `stay`).
props.rotation: Permanent rotation of the paper, in degrees.
props.seed: Random seed for the folds; each number gives a fresh crumple pattern.
props.detail: Mesh density; more means softer folds and heavier computation. Changing it rebuilds the scene.
props.disabled: Disables input and reverts a half-finished crumple.
props.resetKey: Changing it returns the paper to its initial state — for external resets.
props.onError: Called if WebGL is unavailable or the image fails to load; the component falls back to a plain image itself.
props.autoPreview: Automatic crumple preview without any interaction.

tips: This component **does not get RTL, and does not need to**: the 3D scene is symmetric; only the labels and screen-reader states are Persian.

The front image comes from `src` and the back color from `paperColor` — inside the crumple folds the paper's back shows through the creases, so a back color that differs from the image makes the crumpling more legible.
`releaseBehavior="creased"` is great for "notes that get worn": keep `creaseStrength` low so it only creases a little more each time.
With `releaseBehavior="stay"` the paper stays crumpled until you change `resetKey` or the user presses `Escape` — for games and one-off effects.

This component is **the archive's only dynamic-import demo**: `three` is loaded with `next/dynamic` only on this page and the rest of the site stays free of it. If the page feels slow, lower `detail` — fold computation scales with it exponentially.

Motion-sensitive users are not left out either: with `prefers-reduced-motion` the crumple and unfold become instant but the hold and drag logic stays intact, and if WebGL is unavailable it shows a plain image and calls `onError`.
